review_comments.body: ⚠️ Bug: getLoginPredicate change hides linked org brokers on login page The new BROKER_PUBLIC clause was added to the shared `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()`, which is also used by `IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate()` (IdentityProviderBean.java:226) to filter the brokers a user has *already linked* (getFederatedIdentityProviders). Trigger: a realm where organizations are not enabled (feature off or `realm.isOrganizationsEnabled()==false`) but which still has an IDP carrying an organizationId without `kc.org.broker.public=true`, and a user with a federated identity on that IDP — that broker button was rendered before this PR and is now filtered out, so the user can no longer re-authenticate with their linked broker. It also makes `getLoginSearchOptions()` (built from `values()`, no BROKER_PUBLIC entry) and `getLoginPredicate()` describe different rule sets, contradicting the LoginFilter javadoc that the enum contains *all* fields considered for login availability. Keep `getLoginPredicate()` as-is and put the org/public rule in a separate predicate used only by the cache-invalidation helpers. **Keep getLoginPredicate() semantics unchanged and expose the org-public variant separately; then import/use `getForLoginPredicate` instead of `getLoginPredicate` in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider (registerIDPLoginInvalidation / registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate).:** ```` public static Predicate getLoginPredicate() { return ((Predicate) Objects::nonNull) .and(Stream.of(values()).map(LoginFilter::getFilter).reduce(Predicate::and).get()); } /** * Matches exactly the IDPs returned by {@link IdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin}: org-linked IDPs are * only exposed for login when they are public brokers. Used to decide login-cache invalidation. */ public static Predicate getForLoginPredicate() { return getLoginPredicate() .and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))); } ```` - [ ] Apply fix Check the box to apply the fix or reply for a change | Was this helpful? ⚠️ Bug: New test's cleanup uses literal "alias", leaking 21 IDPs `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` registers cleanup for a provider named "alias" instead of the created `idp-alias-`; TestCleanup swallows the resulting NotFoundException, so all 21 providers survive the test. Realms are imported once per class (AbstractKeycloakTest.isImportAfterEachMethod() == false), so leftovers persist across methods: `testCacheIDPByOrg` leaks 10 enabled, `kc.org.broker.public=true` providers whose organizations are then deleted (JpaOrganizationProvider.remove only unlinks IDPs), turning them into realm-level login IDPs — if that method runs first, `assertEquals(5, ...getIDPs(""))` for REALM_ONLY in `testCacheIDPForLogin` fails. Use the real alias in the cleanup registration (both loops). **Register cleanup with the actual alias so the providers are removed after the test.:** ```` for (int i = 0; i < 20; i++) { final String alias = "idp-alias-" + i; IdentityProviderRepresentation idpRep = new IdentityProviderRepresentation(); idpRep.setAlias(alias); ... testRealm().identityProviders().create(idpRep).close(); getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get(alias)::remove); } // ... and for the extra provider created later: getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("idp-alias-20")::remove); ```` - [ ] Apply fix Check the box to apply the fix or reply for a change | Was this helpful? 💡 Performance: remove() now issues an extra DB lookup even when IDP is cached `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` is now executed unconditionally at the start of `remove()`, including the branch where the provider is already in the realm cache (previously the delegate was only hit when the alias key was invalidated). Every IDP deletion therefore pays an additional DB round-trip in a PR whose purpose is to reduce them; the cached `CachedIdentityProvider` already holds the model needed by `registerIDPLoginInvalidation`. **Reuse the cached model when available and only fall back to the delegate lookup otherwise.:** ```` @Override public boolean remove(String alias) { String cacheKey = cacheKeyIdpAlias(getRealm(), alias); CachedIdentityProvider cached = isInvalid(cacheKey) ? null : realmCache.getCache().get(cacheKey, CachedIdentityProvider.class); IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = cached != null ? cached.getIdentityProvider() : idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias); if (storedIdp != null) { registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp); } registerCountInvalidation(); registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp); return idpDelegate.remove(alias); } ```` - [ ] Apply fix Check the box to apply the fix or reply for a change | Was this helpful? ⚠️ Security: Ambiguous classpath no longer fails: equal-order providers pick silently The removed `foundProviders.size() > 1` guard was the only enforcement that exactly one crypto provider is on the classpath, and all three server providers (default, fips1402, elytron) now return the same order `200`. Trigger: a deployment with both keycloak-crypto-default and keycloak-crypto-fips1402 jars — previously an IllegalStateException told the operator to fix the classpath; now `sorted()` is stable so the tie is broken by arbitrary ServiceLoader/classpath order and a FIPS deployment can silently run on the non-FIPS BouncyCastle provider, visible only at debug log level. Keep failing fast when the two highest-order providers share the same `order()` value. **Only tolerate multiple providers when their order values differ, so a genuinely ambiguous classpath still fails fast.:** ```` if (foundProviders.isEmpty()) { throw new IllegalStateException("Not able to load any cryptoProvider with the classLoader: " + classLoader); } if (foundProviders.size() > 1 && foundProviders.get(0).order() == foundProviders.get(1).order()) { throw new IllegalStateException("Multiple crypto providers with the same order loaded with the classLoader: " + classLoader + ". Make sure only one cryptoProvider of a given order is available on the classpath." + " Available providers: " + foundProviders); } logger.debugf("Detected crypto provider: %s", foundProviders.get(0).getClass().getName()); if (foundProviders.size() > 1) { logger.debugf("Ignored crypto providers: %s", foundProviders.subList(1, foundProviders.size())); } return foundProviders.get(0); ```` - [ ] Apply fix Check the box to apply the fix or reply for a change | Was this helpful? 💡 Bug: Dead ASN1Encoder.write() calls in concatenatedRSToASN1DER Lines 114-115 create two throwaway `ASN1Encoder` instances and discard the encoded results; the actual DER is produced by the `writeDerSeq(...)` expression on lines 117-121. These are leftover statements that allocate and encode twice per signature conversion and mislead readers into thinking state is accumulated. Delete them. **Fix:** ```` BigInteger rBigInteger = new BigInteger(r); BigInteger sBigInteger = new BigInteger(s); return ASN1Encoder.create() .writeDerSeq( ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger), ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger)) .toByteArray(); ```` - [ ] Apply fix Check the box to apply the fix or reply for a change | Was this helpful? 💡 Quality: order() added as abstract method breaks external CryptoProvider impls `CryptoProvider` is a public SPI in keycloak-common (consumed by the separate keycloak-client repository and third-party integrations); adding `int order()` as an abstract method makes every out-of-tree implementation fail to compile, and pre-compiled ones throw AbstractMethodError at detection time. The interface already uses default methods (`getSupportedKeyStoreTypes`, `getSupportedRsaKeySizes`), so give `order()` a default so the addition is source- and binary-compatible. **Fix:** ```` /** * Order of this provider. This allows to specify which CryptoProvider will have preference in case that more of them are on the classpath. * * The higher number has preference over the lower number */ default int order() { return 200; } ```` - [ ] Apply fix Check the box to apply the fix or reply for a change | Was this helpful? 💡 Quality: ES384/ES512 tests use a P-256 key, so they never exercise real sizes `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()` uses the JDK default 256-bit curve for all three tests, so for ES384/ES512 the 64-byte signature is zero-padded up to 96/132 bytes by `integerToBytes` and the assertion only verifies that padding round-trips — a real P-384/P-521 signature (where r/s can be 48/66 bytes and DER uses long-form sequence lengths) is never decoded. Generate the key per algorithm curve (secp256r1/secp384r1/secp521r1) so the long-form length and full-width integer paths in ASN1Decoder are actually covered. **Parameterize the curve per ECDSA algorithm instead of relying on the default 256-bit key.:** ```` private void test(ECDSAAlgorithm algorithm, String curve) throws Exception { KeyPairGenerator kpg = KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC"); kpg.initialize(new java.security.spec.ECGenParameterSpec(curve)); KeyPair keyPair = kpg.genKeyPair(); AuthzClientCryptoProvider prov = new AuthzClientCryptoProvider(); // ... rest unchanged, using the local keyPair } @Test public void testES256() throws Exception { test(ECDSAAlgorithm.ES256, "secp256r1"); } @Test public void testES384() throws Exception { test(ECDSAAlgorithm.ES384, "secp384r1"); } @Test public void testES512() throws Exception { test(ECDSAAlgorithm.ES512, "secp521r1"); } ```` - [ ] Apply fix Check the box to apply the fix or reply for a change | Was this helpful? 💡 Quality: Ignored-provider message built unconditionally and passed as format string The StringBuilder is assembled on every `detectProvider` call even when debug logging is off, and the result is handed to `logger.debugf(...)` as the *format* string (so any `%` in the text would go through String.format) with a trailing ", " separator. Log the list directly with a `%s` placeholder instead. **Fix:** ```` if (foundProviders.size() > 1 && logger.isDebugEnabled()) { logger.debugf("Ignored crypto providers: %s", foundProviders.subList(1, foundProviders.size()).stream() .map(p -> p.getClass().getName()) .collect(Collectors.joining(", "))); } ```` - [ ] Apply fix Check the box to apply the fix or reply for a change | Was this helpful? ⚠️ Bug: isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is always False for spawn procs Flusher processes are created with `self.mp_context = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")`, so real processes are `SpawnProcess` instances. `multiprocessing.Process` resolves to the default context's base `Process` class (fork/forkserver on Linux), which `SpawnProcess` does not subclass, so `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is always False for the actual worker processes. As a result the newly-added guard in `_ensure_processes_alive` never calls `process.kill()`: a hung ("hang" cause) process is left running while a replacement is spawned, leaking processes and Redis connections and risking duplicate segment production to Kafka. The same guard in `join()` means `terminate()` never runs either. The previous single-process code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally, so this is a regression. Use a check that matches spawn processes, e.g. `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess)` or `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)`. **Kill only real (non-thread) processes; threads have no kill(). Apply the same isinstance change to the terminate() call in join().:** ```` try: if not isinstance(process, threading.Thread): process.kill() except (ValueError, AttributeError): pass # Process already closed, ignore ```` - [ ] Apply fix Check the box to apply the fix or reply for a change | Was this helpful?
